title: Church Leadership
definition: Church leadership is the God-given responsibility of qualified leaders to shepherd, teach, guard, and serve the people of God under Christ's authority.
summary: Church leaders are called to shepherd God's people faithfully under the authority of Christ and Scripture.
christFocus: Jesus is the Chief Shepherd, and all church leadership must reflect His truth, humility, care, and authority.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Church leadership is not about personal platform or control. Leaders are called to shepherd God's people, teach sound doctrine, guard against error, equip the saints, and serve as examples.

Scripture gives qualifications for leaders because the care of souls is serious. Character matters as much as ability. Leaders must be faithful in doctrine, humble in conduct, and watchful in service.

All church leadership is under Christ. He is the head of the Church and the Chief Shepherd. Faithful leaders point people to Him, not to themselves.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Poor leadership can wound people, distort doctrine, and damage the witness of the Church. This doctrine matters because God's people need shepherds who are faithful, humble, qualified, and accountable to Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Pray for church leaders, test teaching by Scripture, and honor faithful shepherding. If you lead, serve with humility and fear of God, remembering that the flock belongs to Christ.
